rows.ID: PHASE A - Placement of Ipsilateral Wire and Contralateral Catheter

rows.Description: Let's begin by setting up the ipsilateral and contralateral femoral access.
rows.Required data: Procedure started event.

rows.Description: Ultrasound-guided retrograde bilateral femoral access. 6Fr introducer, double Proglide prepositioning per side, 10 Fr sheath.
rows.Notes: Suitable navigational wires, eg, J-tip guidewires, advanced into the abdominal aorta.

rows.Context / Step: Insert standard guidewire on left side
rows.Description: Insert the standard guidewire from the left access.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_seen; required_family: guidewire; required_stiffness: standard; access_scope: left
rows.Notes: Keep left and right access distinct until the stiff guidewire establishes the ipsilateral side (prob. this will be fixed from the pre-planning sheet).

rows.Context / Step: Insert standard guidewire on right side
rows.Description: Insert the standard guidewire from the right access.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_seen; required_family: guidewire; required_stiffness: standard; access_scope: right

rows.Context / Step: Catheter insertion and advancement via the Ipsilateral Side
rows.Description: A suitable catheter (eg, Berenstein) is passed over the ipsilateral J-tip wire and the two are advanced into the thoracic aorta to ensure non-traumatic access. First guidewire into the thoracic aorta, then catheter.

A pigtail catheter is inserted via the contralateral femoral artery and over the J-tip wire and positioned with the tip curled just above the renal artery level (usually just above the L1-L2 disc space).

rows.Context / Step: Insert protective catheter on left side
rows.Description: Insert a protective catheter from the left access.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_seen; required_family: catheter; access_scope: left
rows.Notes: The runtime accepts generic catheter-family evidence for the protective catheter on each side.

rows.Context / Step: Insert protective catheter on right side
rows.Description: Insert a protective catheter from the right access.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_seen; required_family: catheter; access_scope: right

rows.Description: The J-tip wire is withdrawn from the contralateral side to prepare for angiographic planning.

rows.Context / Step: Remove standard guidewire from left side
rows.Description: Remove the standard guidewire from the left access.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_removed_after_seen; required_family: guidewire; required_stiffness: standard; access_scope: left

rows.Context / Step: Guide Wire Exchange via Ipsilateral Side
rows.Description: The ipsilateral J-tip wire is exchanged for a stiff guidewire (eg, Lunderquist) that will support the stent graft delivery system.

rows.Context / Step: Insert stiff guidewire on the chosen ipsilateral side
rows.Description: Insert the stiff guidewire through the ipsilateral access before removing that protective catheter.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_seen; required_family: guidewire; required_stiffness: stiff; access_scope: ipsilateral
rows.Notes: The access used for this stiff guidewire establishes the ipsilateral side (prob. this will be taken from the pre-planning sheet); leave its protective catheter in place during the exchange.

rows.Description: Warning. It is safer to introduce the ipsilateral stiff guidewire through a protective catheter to reduce the risk of vessel rupture.
rows.Notes: This is triggered when ipsilateral stiff-wire exchange without protective catheter evidence.

rows.Description: The catheter is removed from the ipsilateral side, leaving the stiff (Lunderquist) wire positioned at the distal aortic arch.

rows.Context / Step: Remove protective catheter from ipsilateral side
rows.Description: Remove the ipsilateral protective catheter after the stiff guidewire is in place.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_removed_after_seen; required_family: catheter; access_scope: ipsilateral
rows.Notes: Remove only the protective catheter on the ipsilateral side..

rows.Description: Phase A milestones have been completed. Please now review the checks list.
C-arm movement to visualise the angulation of the lowest renal artery.

rows.Context / Step: Check vital signs for any indication of access-site rupture.
rows.Description: Review the patient's vital signs and overall hemodynamic trend to exclude an access-site rupture after femoral access. Tachycardia, hypotension, or other instability at this stage should prompt immediate reassessment before proceeding.
rows.Notes: Check alert: Check vital signs to rule out access-site rupture before continuing.

rows.Context / Step: Check for cardiac arrhythmia if any wire or catheter advances too far.
rows.Description: Unexpected deep advancement of a wire or catheter can enter the ventricle and trigger tachycardia or ectopy. This remains a surgeon-facing awareness prompt unless real-time vital-sign data become available from the simulator.
rows.Notes: Check alert: If a wire or catheter advances too far, check heart rate to exclude ventricular irritation.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the stiff guidewire reaches the aorta or thoracic aorta only on the ipsilateral side.
rows.Description: This step verifies that the exchanged stiff guidewire provides stable support for the main-body delivery system. The intended result is one appropriate stiff wire in the aorta or thoracic aorta through the ipsilateral access, without an unnecessary second stiff wire.
rows.Required data: Tool identity/family, anatomical region, multiplicity.
rows.Notes: Configured target is Thoracic Aorta.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the C-arm angle is optimised to visualise the lowest renal artery.
rows.Description: The C-arm view should clearly open the lowest renal artery so the proximal landing zone can be judged without ambiguity. A precise projection at this point reduces the risk of covering a renal artery or accepting an inaccurate deployment level.
rows.Required data: Live C-arm angles; runtime-side preplanning target; configured tolerance.
rows.Notes: angulationPlan.renal_lao_raoangulationPlan.renal_cra_cau

rows.Context / Step: Check that the pigtail catheter is placed above the renal level on the contralateral side.
rows.Description: The contralateral pigtail catheter should be positioned just above the renal artery level so the angiographic roadmap remains trustworthy. If it sits too low or on the wrong side, positioning decisions for the main body become less reliable.
rows.Required data: Tool identity/family, anatomical region, multiplicity; runtime access side.
rows.Notes: Runtime contralateral side; supported pigtail/marker catheter in Suprarenal Region.Check alert: Keep the pigtail catheter curled just above the renal level on the contralateral side to obtain a reliable roadmap.

rows.ID: The below alerts arise when triggered during the whole procedure.

rows.Description: A procedural tool has moved above the subclavian artery outside the thoracic aorta. Reposition it immediately.
rows.Required data: Tool enters above-subclavian danger region.
rows.Notes: Preventive alerts

rows.Description: A procedural tool has entered the renal artery region. Remove or reposition it immediately.
rows.Required data: Tool enters renal-artery region.

rows.Description: A procedural tool has entered the celiac trunk region. Reposition it immediately.
rows.Required data: Tool enters celiac region.

rows.Description: A procedural tool has entered the superior mesenteric artery region. Reposition it immediately.
rows.Required data: Tool enters superior-mesenteric region.

rows.Description: A procedural tool has entered a dangerous critical zone. Reposition it immediately [GENERAL].
rows.Required data: Tool enters critical danger region.

rows.ID: PHASE B - Insertion and Positioning of Main Body

rows.Description: Let's proceed to Phase B. Select the prosthesis according to the pre-planning recommendation.
The prosthesis-selection check is accessible at the beginning of Phase B.
rows.Required data: rule_type: always_accessible; access_scope: any
rows.Notes: The prosthesis-selection check is accessible at the beginning of Phase B. Unlocks: B-C01.

rows.Description: Select the main body according to the case-specific preplanning and applicable device instructions.
rows.Notes: ~20% oversizing claim; case/device-specific sizing requires expert review.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the selected main body matches the pre-planning recommendation.
rows.Description: Before the delivery system is introduced, compare the selected main-body graft with the preplanning recommendation. This prevents committing to an inappropriate main-body diameter or length for the proximal and ipsilateral distal landing zones.
rows.Required data: Selected component code and applicable preplanning code(s).
rows.Notes: Check on prothesys.trunk_ipsi.code.Check alert: Confirm the selected main body matches the planned prosthesis before introduction.

rows.Description: The selected prosthesis does not match the pre-planning recommendation. Review the displayed recommendation before continuing.
rows.Notes: This can recur for later component selections, not only Phase B.

rows.Description: Advance the device to the aneurysm neck.
rows.Notes: Unlocked by Main-body selection and B-C01 resolved.

rows.Description: Thread the delivery system with the main body over the stiff guide wire (Lunderquist) on the ipsilateral side. The delivery system should be wetted before it enters the vessel to activate the hydrophilic coating.

Using the front grip, advance the delivery system with the main body until the proximal end markers of the stent graft are level with the proximal landing zone level below the lowest renal artery. Rotational alignment should be adjusted to ensure the contralateral limb gate will open towards the contralateral access side
rows.Notes: Proximal marker telemetry is implemented. Runtime unlocks B-C03/B-C04/B-C02 when the main body reaches the aneurysm neck.

rows.Context / Step: Unlock second part of Phase B
rows.Description: Unlock marker positioning, gate orientation, and contrast planning when the main body reaches the aneurysm neck.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_seen; required_tool_code: Trunk-Ipsilateral Leg; required_family: prothesis; access_scope: any; required_anatomical_region: Neck of the Aneurysm
rows.Notes: Unlocks: B-C03;B-C04;B-C02 when the main body reaches the aneurysm neck.

rows.Description: Review the checklist for proximal marker position and contralateral gate orientation.
rows.Required data: Main body reaches neck region and positioning block becomes available.

rows.Context / Step: Position the proximal main-body marker immediately below the renal bifurcation.
rows.Description: The intended proximal-marker position is below the renal bifurcation. The automated proximity check accepts a reported renal distance of at most the configured tolerance in magnitude and does not by itself verify which side of the renal reference the marker occupies. Confirm the below-renal position manually.
rows.Required data: Main-body proximal-marker or landmark distance; renal reference; configured tolerance.
rows.Notes: !!!!! to do (uncalibrated)Tolerance can be set in config.yaml. Continuous monitoring stops at 30% main-body deployment. Check alert: Position the proximal marker within the configured landing window below the lowest renal artery.

rows.Description: After B-C03 is resolved, choose between a crossed-limb ballerina configuration or the default configuration.
rows.Required data: rule_type: always_accessible; related checks: B-C04
rows.Notes: This is an explicit popup choice (with buttons) before the contralateral-gate orientation check.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the contralateral gate is oriented toward the contralateral access side.
rows.Description: Before deployment progresses, confirm that the main body is rotated so the contralateral gate opens toward the contralateral access. Correct orientation reduces difficult cannulation and unnecessary catheter manipulation later.
rows.Notes: Manual orientation assessment; dynamic w.r.t. setup chosen in B-M03.Check alert: Orient the contralateral gate toward the contralateral side before further deployment.

rows.Description: Danger. Main-body deployment has started before the proximal marker position and contralateral gate orientation checks are complete. Pause deployment and complete checks B-C03 and B-C04.
rows.Notes: Safety alert;First observed deployment above 0% while B-C03 or B-C04 is unresolved.

rows.Context / Step: Check the contrast injection rate and volume before the initial aortogram.
rows.Description: This is the final Phase B review before angiography. Confirm that contrast rate and volume are appropriate for adequate renal visualization while limiting unnecessary contrast load.
rows.Notes: Check alert: Verify contrast rate and volume before the first angiogram and keep the patient's renal reserve in mind.

rows.Description: Visualize the renal arteries and confirm the main-body position.
rows.Notes: Selected main body and B-C01/B-C03/B-C04/B-C02 resolved; waits for angiography evidence.

rows.Description: Danger. Contrast injection was reported before the required angiography preparation was complete. Review catheter positioning and complete the preparation steps before another injection.
rows.Required data: Explicit contrast-injection event before the active Phase B or Phase G preparation requirements are resolved.
rows.Notes: Safety alert; can be triggered every time an angio is performed.

rows.Description: Contrast is injected to visualise the renal arteries, and image overlay is used to fine-tune positioning just below the lowest renal artery.

rows.ID: PHASE C - Deployment of Main Body and Ipsilateral Limb

rows.Description: Start main-body deployment by turning the deployment device knob counterclockwise.
rows.Required data: Entry to main-body deployment after Phase B angiography.

rows.Description: Begin deployment by retracting the outer sheath until the proximal covered stent rings are partially opened.
rows.Notes: All the steps in this script are written for medtronic prosthesis so some steps can be unnecessary if working with EVAR default module on the simulator (GORE prosthesis).

rows.Description: The proximal graft markers are above the renal bifurcation landmark. Reposition the main body below the renal arteries.
rows.Required data: Conditional during the relevant positioning/withdrawal activity; not a scheduled step. Catalogue definition for proximal marker above renal reference; automatic emission path not confirmed in current code.
rows.Notes: TODO!!!!! Doesn’t workPreventive alert; Catalogue presence does not establish runtime activation.

rows.Description: Adjust the graft position and rotation before further deployment, ensuring proximal apposition and correct contralateral gate orientation.
rows.Notes: This is the last phase where meaningful repositioning is still possible before definitive anchoring.

rows.Context / Step: Keep the proximal main-body marker in the renal landing window during deployment.
rows.Description: The configured signed renal-distance window is -10 to 0 mm. This check uses available marker or main-body landmark distance and direction information to monitor proximity below the renal reference. Confirm the anatomical marker position manually.
rows.Required data: Main-body marker or landmark distance and direction; renal reference.
rows.Notes: !!!!! to do (uncalibrated)The check reopens if the evaluated position moves outside the configured window. Get a new reminder after 15% of deployment.

rows.Description: Continue deployment until the contralateral limb gate is opened, then deploy the proximal bare stent to anchor the graft in the proximal neck.
Stop as soon as the contralateral gate is released.
rows.Notes: Main-body deployment continues toward the configured contralateral-gate release threshold (fixed to 50% deployment, maybe better 55%).

rows.Description: Keep main-body deployment paused.
rows.Required data: Contralateral gate reaches its release threshold.
rows.Notes: Popup title: Begin contralateral-leg cannulation.

rows.Description: Danger. Main-body deployment has continued beyond contralateral gate release before the pigtail test is resolved. Pause deployment and confirm or dismiss check D-C01 before continuing.
rows.Required data: First observed deployment above the gate-release threshold while D-C01 is unresolved.
rows.Notes: Safety alert

rows.Context / Step: Ipsilateral limb deployment and distal apposition
rows.Description: Deploy the ipsilateral limb and position the distal marker with respect to the ipsilateral iliac landing zone / iliac bifurcation.

rows.Context / Step: Apposition of the ipsilateral distal end of stent graft
rows.Description: Land the radio-opaque marker of the graft cover as it is retracted so that it sits 1 cm past the distal end of the graft material.
rows.Notes: not validated by current codeMoved before delivery-system withdrawal.

rows.Description: The distal main-body marker has gone below the iliac landing limit. Reposition the prosthesis above the iliac half line.
rows.Required data: Conditional during the relevant positioning/withdrawal activity; not a scheduled step. Catalogue only: no implemented distal-marker check in current checklist; automatic trigger not established.
rows.Notes: probably uselessPreventive alert

rows.Description: Continue until deployment reaches 100%.
rows.Required data: Shown after the relevant intermediate checks are resolved.
rows.Notes: These alerts are assigned for coherence to phase C (main body deployment), but with the new procedure (contra cannulation BEFORE complete deploy of main body) they’re used in phase D.

rows.Description: Main body deployment is complete. Withdraw the delivery system, paying attention to the final checks.
rows.Required data: Main-body deployment reaches 100%, before delivery-system withdrawal.

rows.Description: Danger. A delivery system has been removed before full deployment was recorded. Stop and review the device deployment status before continuing.
rows.Required data: Tracked main-body, contralateral-limb, iliac-extender, or aortic-extender device removed before its recorded deployment peak reaches 100%.
rows.Notes: probably useless

rows.Context / Step: Nose cone recapture and delivery system withdrawal
rows.Description: Recapture the nose cone, reunite the nose cone and graft cover, and withdraw the delivery system under fluoroscopic control while maintaining wire position.
rows.Notes: Only on medtronic prosthesis. NO prob for simulator

rows.Description: The stiff guidewire has left the thoracic aorta and entered a dangerous region. Reposition the guidewire in the thoracic aorta.
rows.Required data: Conditional during the relevant positioning/withdrawal activity; not a scheduled step. Monitored stiff wire leaves thoracic aorta for a configured danger region.
rows.Notes: Preventive alert; suppressed by current no_safety_alerts=true.

rows.Description: The guidewire has moved down into the suprarenal region during delivery-system withdrawal. Pause withdrawal and restore the guidewire tip to the thoracic aorta while maintaining wire control.
rows.Required data: Stiff guidewire leaves the thoracic aorta during delivery-system withdrawal.
rows.Notes: Safety alert.

rows.ID: PHASE D - Contralateral Cannulation and Main-Body Completion

rows.Description: Advance the angled catheter and guidewire into the suprarenal region.
rows.Required data: D-M01, D-M02 and D-M03 completed after the main-body pause.
rows.Notes: Maybe it’s a bit out of scope bcs before we have to withdraw the pigtail.

rows.Description: Withdraw the contralateral pigtail, then insert an angled catheter and a soft or stiff guidewire from the contralateral access.
Withdraw the contralateral Pigtail Catheter or Pigtail Marker Catheter.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_removed_after_seen; required_tool_code: Pigtail Catheter;Pigtail Marker Catheter; required_family: catheter; access_scope: contralateral
rows.Notes: Triggered directly by the contralateral pigtail OUT event after the 50% main-body pause.

rows.Description: Insert an angled catheter from the contralateral side for gate cannulation.
An angled catheter is suggested for contralateral gate cannulation.
rows.Required data: Non-angled catheter encountered inserted during contralateral cannulation.

rows.Description: Insert an angled catheter suitable for contralateral gate cannulation.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_seen; required_tool_code: configured angled catheters; required_family: catheter; access_scope: contralateral
rows.Notes: Triggered directly by a valid contralateral angled-catheter IN event after D-M01.

rows.Description: Insert a soft or stiff guidewire from the contralateral side for gate cannulation.
rows.Required data: rule_type: tool_seen; required_family: guidewire; access_scope: contralateral
rows.Notes: probably only a soft guidewire is suggested here.Triggered directly by a contralateral guidewire IN event after D-M02. Once D-M01 to D-M03 are complete, D-A02 is shown.

rows.Description: Cannulate the contralateral gate, then advance both the angled catheter and guidewire until both tips reach the suprarenal region.
When both the contralateral angled-catheter tip and guidewire tip are in the suprarenal region, proceed to the pigtail exchange and circular test.

rows.Context / Step: Replace the angled catheter with a pigtail
rows.Description: Maintain guidewire access through the gate, withdraw the angled catheter, and insert a pigtail inside the main body for the circular pigtail test.
Place the pigtail inside the main body and perform the circular test.
rows.Required data: Angled catheter and guidewire have reached the suprarenal region; begin the pigtail exchange/test.

rows.Context / Step: Confirm true intragraft cannulation using the pigtail rotation test.
rows.Description: Once the angled catheter and guidewire have both reached the suprarenal region, exchange the angled catheter for a contralateral pigtail. Insert the pigtail inside the main body and perform the manual circular movement test under fluoroscopy to confirm true intragraft position.
rows.Notes: Resolving D-C01 arms the post-test stiff-guidewire gate but does not resume main-body deployment by itself. A stiff guidewire already present before D-C01 is resolved does not count.

rows.Description: Reinsert a Lunderquist or another stiff guidewire through the contralateral pigtail and advance it to the thoracic aorta.
rows.Required data: D-C01 resolved; the contralateral pigtail has reached the aneurysm neck after angled-catheter cannulation.

rows.Description: After resolving D-C01, reinsert a Lunderquist or another stiff guidewire through the contralateral pigtail and advance that same newly inserted wire to the thoracic aorta before resuming main-body deployment.

rows.Context / Step: Verify that the distal main-body landing preserves internal iliac blood flow.
rows.Description: The current stream does not identify the distal end of the deployed main body. Verify the distal landing manually on fluoroscopy, keeping it above the iliac half-line at the intended ipsilateral level and clear of the internal iliac origin.
rows.Notes: Unlocks at CC02_depl_thresh (configured at 85%) after D-C01 is resolved and the fresh contralateral stiff guidewire has reached the thoracic aorta. Manual distal-landing assessment; do not substitute catheter, wire or proximal-tip position.

rows.Description: During withdrawal of the delivery system, pay close attention that the nose cone and capture basket do not snag or become trapped inside the endograft.
rows.Required data: Operator assessment.
rows.Notes: This is checked only when prosthesis_type: medtronic.Unlocks at 100% main-body deployment after cannulation is completed, including the post-test stiff-guidewire gate.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the stiff guidewire remains safely in the thoracic aorta during delivery-system withdrawal.
rows.Description: During and after withdrawal of the main-body delivery system, the stiff guidewire should remain in the thoracic aorta. Entering the region above the subclavian artery, the suprarenal region, the superior mesenteric artery, or the celiac trunk should trigger immediate repositioning.
rows.Notes: Unlocks at 100% main-body deployment after cannulation is completed, including the post-test stiff-guidewire gate; live guidewire monitoring continues during withdrawal (if changes region an alert is sent).

rows.Context / Step: Check final main-body stability after delivery-system withdrawal.
rows.Description: This remains a prompt-info reminder for now: once the delivery system is out, visually confirm once more that the main body has remained stable and has not migrated from the landing positions obtained during deployment.
rows.Required data: Operator assessment.
rows.Notes: Unlocks at 100% main-body deployment after cannulation is completed, including the post-test stiff-guidewire gate.

rows.ID: PHASE E - Insertion and Positioning of Contralateral Limb

rows.Description: Set up the C-arm to visualize the contralateral iliac bifurcation and select the planned contralateral limb.
rows.Required data: Entry to Phase E.

rows.Description: C-arm adjusted to visualise the iliac bifurcation.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the C-arm is adjusted to visualise the contralateral iliac bifurcation.
rows.Description: Adjust the C-arm so the contralateral iliac bifurcation is well profiled before positioning the limb. A clear view is required to judge the distal landing accurately and to preserve the intended iliac branches.
Withdraw the shaped (vertebral) catheter and insert an appropriate-size sheath (eg, 16 Fr) via the contralateral access. Advance the sheath to land at the contralateral iliac bif.
A contrast injection is performed to identify the iliac bifurcation and confirm an adequate landing zone for the limb extension.
Select correct contralateral prosthesis.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the selected contralateral limb matches one of the compatible pre-planning recommendations.
rows.Description: Before introduction, compare the selected contralateral limb with both compatible pre-planning options. Either recommended code is valid for this patient; any other selection should be corrected before continuing.
rows.Required data: Selected component code and applicable preplanning code(s).

rows.Description: Advance it into the main body.
rows.Required data: Triggered when E-C01/E-C02 resolved and simulator confirms contralateral-limb selection.
rows.Notes: Popup title: Insert the contralateral limb.

rows.Description: The contralateral limb graft of appropriate dimensions is advanced into position, while keeping the stiff wire under control. Proceed with attention to the limb graft's proximal marker, the overlap marker in relation to the contralateral limb gate..
Contralateral limb on the wrong side. Insert it through the contralateral access.
rows.Required data: Contralateral limb detected on incorrect access side.

rows.Description: Check the positioning of the proximal overlap marker and the distal landing marker before deployment.
rows.Required data: Contralateral limb reaches the required neck region.
rows.Notes: Introduces the checks E-C03 and E-C04.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the contralateral limb overlap marker is aligned with the contralateral gate before deployment.
rows.Description: The contralateral limb should be advanced so that its overlap marker aligns correctly with the contralateral gate. Proper overlap is critical for sealing the junction and avoiding a weak or insufficient component connection.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the planned distal landing will preserve internal iliac flow before contralateral limb deployment.
rows.Description: Before deployment of the contralateral limb, verify that the intended distal landing preserves internal iliac flow. This prompt protects against avoidable hypogastric coverage and pelvic ischemic complications.

rows.ID: PHASE F - Deployment of Contralateral Limb

rows.Description: Keep the delivery system stable while rotating the grip.
The graft is deployed using controlled rotation of the deployment grip (blue) while keeping the delivery system (grey) in a fixed position.
rows.Notes: Deployment percentage is available; automatic distal-marker and stability verification is not implemented.

rows.Description: Check that the delivery system remains stable during deployment.
rows.Required data: Triggered when contralateral deployment reaches 15% to introduce check F-C01.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the delivery system remains stable while the contralateral limb is deployed.
rows.Description: During deployment of the contralateral limb, the delivery system should remain fixed while the deployment grip is rotated. Unintended motion at release can compromise both overlap and distal landing.
rows.Notes: Deployment >=15% unlocks this manual check.

rows.Description: Continue the deployment until the limb is fully opened.
rows.Required data: F-C01 resolved while deployment remains below 100%.

rows.Description: Confirm that the graft is fully open. Then the nose cone is reunited with the stent cover, by use of the trigger allowing the rear grip (blue) to be held stationary while the front grip (grey) is retreated caudally.
Begin withdrawing the contralateral delivery system while maintaining guidewire control and prosthesis stability.
rows.Required data: Contralateral deployment reaches 100%.

rows.Context / Step: Withdrawal of the contralateral delivery system
rows.Description: The system is then carefully withdrawn under fluoroscopic control while the wire is kept stable, and using an alternating torque motion to ease passage without displacing the graft.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the contralateral delivery system is withdrawn while guidewire stability is maintained.
rows.Description: After the limb is fully opened and the nose cone is recaptured, the contralateral delivery system should be withdrawn under fluoroscopic control while keeping the wire stable.
rows.Notes: Probably these can be turned into ToolWithdrawnCheck.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the contralateral limb remains stable after deployment and system withdrawal.
rows.Description: After deployment and delivery-system withdrawal, re-evaluate the contralateral limb to confirm that overlap and distal landing are still intact before moving on.
Would you add an iliac extender? Review the iliac landing and decide whether an extender is required before proceeding.
rows.Required data: Shown after simulator-confirmed contralateral delivery-device withdrawal. first contralateral side and then the ipsilateral side.
rows.Notes: A popup with buttons. A choice that disagrees with pre-planning requires a second confirmation.

rows.Description: Pre-planning recommends an iliac extender. Review the planned component carefully before proceeding.
rows.Required data: Shown beside the intended decision branch.

rows.Description: Pre-planning recommends an iliac extender. Are you sure you want to proceed without it?
rows.Required data: Conditional confirmation shown when the operator declines an extender recommended by pre-planning.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the selected iliac extender matches the pre-planning recommendation.
rows.Description: If an extender is chosen, review the selected component against the plan when one exists; use the manual selection branch for an unplanned extender.
rows.Required data: Selected component code and applicable preplanning code(s).
rows.Notes: CONTRALATERAL SIDE

rows.Description: Advance it toward the planned landing zone.
rows.Required data: Iliac extender selected and F-C04 resolved; await insertion on the current side.

rows.Description: Introduce the iliac extender.

For each side in sequence (contralateral first, then ipsilateral), decide whether an iliac extender is required. If selected, review the component, introduce it, confirm its position, deploy it fully, and withdraw its delivery device.
rows.Notes: F-C04 and F-C05 reset for the second side; the UI preserves the first side's outcome.

rows.Description: First confirm the extender is positioned correctly.
rows.Required data: Current-side iliac extender inserted and F-C05 resolved; begin deployment.

rows.Context / Step: Check iliac extender positioning before deployment.
rows.Description: After inserting the iliac extender, confirm adequate overlap with the previous limb, the intended distal landing, internal iliac artery preservation, and stable positioning before starting deployment.
rows.Notes: Unlocked immediately after insertion at 0% deployment. Resolving this check opens the deployment prompt.

rows.Description: Continue until deployment reaches 100%.
rows.Required data: Current deployment popup remains active until 100%.

rows.Description: Withdraw the iliac extender deployment device.
rows.Required data: Current-side iliac-extender deployment reaches 100%; await delivery-device removal.

rows.ID: REPEAT SAME PROCEDURE FOR THE IPSILATERAL SIDE

rows.Context / Step: Check that the selected iliac extender matches the pre-planning recommendation.
rows.Description: If an extender is chosen, review the selected component against the plan when one exists; use the manual selection branch for an unplanned extender.
rows.Required data: Selected component code and applicable preplanning code(s).
rows.Notes: IPSILATERAL SIDE

rows.Context / Step: Check iliac extender positioning before deployment.
rows.Description: After inserting the iliac extender, confirm adequate overlap with the previous limb, the intended distal landing, internal iliac artery preservation, and stable positioning before starting deployment.
rows.Notes: Unlocked immediately after insertion at 0% deployment. Resolving this check opens the deployment prompt.

rows.Description: After both iliac sides are decided, review whether an aortic extender is required. If selected, confirm the component against preplanning, insert it, review positioning and overlap, deploy to 100%, and withdraw the delivery device.
rows.Notes: Phase G remains locked until every selected extender is fully deployed and its delivery device is removed.

rows.Description: Would you add an aortic extender?
rows.Required data: Both iliac-extender side decisions are complete.

rows.Description: Pre-planning recommends an aortic extender. Are you sure you want to proceed without it?
rows.Required data: Conditional: No when an aortic extender is planned.

rows.Description: Pre-planning does not predict that an aortic extender is necessary. Confirm whether you still want to introduce one.
rows.Required data: Conditional: Yes when no aortic extender is planned.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the selected aortic extender matches the pre-planning recommendation.
rows.Description: If an aortic extender is required, confirm that the selected component matches the pre-planning recommendation before introduction and deployment.
rows.Required data: Selected component code and applicable aortic-extender preplanning code.
rows.Notes: A planned aortic extender is verified against its component code. If no extender was planned but the operator confirms one, this check unlocks immediately as a manual review/dismissal check so the workflow can continue.

rows.Description: Start aortic extender insertion.
rows.Required data: Aortic extender selected and F-C08 resolved; await insertion.

rows.Context / Step: Check aortic extender positioning before deployment.
rows.Description: After inserting the aortic extender, confirm adequate overlap with the main body, the intended seal zone, and stable positioning before starting deployment.
rows.Notes: Unlocked immediately after aortic-extender insertion at 0% deployment. Resolving this check opens the deployment prompt.

rows.Description: Confirm the aortic extender is correctly positioned, then begin deployment.
rows.Required data: F-C09 resolved and aortic-extender deployment remains below 100%.

rows.Description: Withdraw the aortic extender deployment device.
rows.Required data: Aortic-extender deployment reaches 100%; await simulator-confirmed delivery-device removal.

rows.Description: Position the pigtail catheter for the completion angiogram.
rows.Required data: Entry to Phase G; position pigtail.

rows.Description: Position the c-arm for the completion angiogram.
rows.Notes: make a check for correct C-Arm positioning

rows.Description: Choosing whichever side is most convenient, a pigtail catheter is inserted to allow final angiographic assessment with contrast released just above the renal artery level - its guide wire having been retracted to allow the pigtail to form visibly.

rows.Context / Step: Check that the pigtail or marker catheter is positioned just above the renal arteries for the completion angiogram.
rows.Description: For the completion angiogram, the pigtail or marker catheter should sit just above the renal artery level so contrast gives a dependable overview of the proximal seal and the main branches.
rows.Required data: Tool identity/family, anatomical region, multiplicity.

rows.Description: Withdraw the stiff wire from the other side to below the stent bifurcation to allow the iliac limbs to take their natural shape.
Assess graft position, iliac flow, and possible endoleaks.
rows.Required data: G-C01 resolved; waits for a newer initial Phase G angiography event.

rows.Description: A final angiogram using contrast should confirm that: the main stent graft position is below the renal arteries, preservation of bilateral internal iliac flows, and absence of endoleaks.

rows.Context / Step: Check the final angiogram for correct graft position, bilateral internal iliac flow, and absence of endoleaks.
rows.Description: Interpret the completion angiogram systematically, confirming that the main body remains below the renal arteries, both internal iliac arteries are preserved, and no endoleak is visible. This is the final global technical assessment of the repair.
rows.Notes: Manual image interpretation. No implemented angiogram anomaly/endoleak-recognition model (probably a future work - post-op agent).

rows.Description: Insert the stent-graft balloon through the ipsilateral access to begin balloon moulding.
rows.Required data: Initial Phase G angiography recorded and G-C02 resolved; begin the required ipsilateral balloon-moulding sequence.

rows.Description: Use the stent-graft balloon on the ipsilateral side at the proximal anchoring zone and ipsilateral iliac landing zone. Then remove and reinsert it through the contralateral access for proximal anchoring, main-body-to-limb overlap, and contralateral iliac landing inflations.
rows.Required data: Inflation-start and deflation-end events; exactly one sided balloon present; region-specific milestones latched for each access side.
rows.Notes: The ipsilateral side requires two inflation locations. The contralateral side requires three, including the aneurysm-region overlap.This logic currently doesn’t take into account the extenders (maybe would be useful?)Bilateral balloon removal opens G-M01 to G-M03 for the final angiogram.

rows.Description: Inflate the balloon at the proximal graft anchoring zone near the renal arteries and at the ipsilateral iliac landing zone.
rows.Required data: Balloon detected on the ipsilateral side before both required inflations are recorded.

rows.Description: Deflate and withdraw the balloon, then reinsert it through the contralateral access.
rows.Required data: Ipsilateral balloon milestones are complete and the balloon is removed.

rows.Description: Inflate the balloon at the proximal graft anchoring zone near the renal arteries, at the overlap between the main body and contralateral limb, and at the contralateral iliac landing zone.
rows.Required data: Balloon detected on the contralateral side before all three required inflations are recorded.

rows.Description: Prepare for final angiogram.
rows.Required data: Bilateral balloon removal is complete and no balloon remains present.

rows.Context / Step: Insert one catheter on one side (left or right)
rows.Description: Insert one new catheter on one side only after bilateral balloon removal.
rows.Required data: rule_type: always_accessible; required_family: catheter; access_scope: any; min_count: 1
rows.Notes: A catheter already present before the final milestone panel opens does not count.

rows.Context / Step: Remove the guidewire from the catheter side
rows.Description: Withdraw the guidewire on the same side after the new catheter has been inserted.
rows.Required data: rule_type: always_accessible; required_family: guidewire; access_scope: same side as G-M01
rows.Notes: Withdrawal on the opposite side does not count. Reinsertion blocks angiography until the guidewire is withdrawn again.

rows.Description: Perform a subsequent final angiogram with the new catheter still present and its same-side guidewire withdrawn.
rows.Required data: rule_type: always_accessible; evidence: angiography after G-M02
rows.Notes: Earlier angiograms do not count. Completion unlocks the final review and KPI report.

rows.Description: After bilateral balloon moulding, insert one new catheter on one side only, remove the guidewire from that same side, and perform a subsequent final angiogram while the catheter remains present.
rows.Required data: G-M01, G-M02 and G-M03 in order.
rows.Notes: Earlier catheters, guidewire withdrawals, and angiograms do not satisfy this final sequence.

rows.Description: Review the final angiogram and simulation summary.
rows.Required data: G-M03 completed after the ordered final catheter and guidewire milestones.
rows.Notes: Download of the report is available.
